title: GTA VI HDR and TV Setup: PS5 and Xbox Checklist
summary: Prepare your television's game mode, HDR calibration and display settings before GTA VI launches.
intro: Before GTA VI's scheduled November 19, 2026 launch, players can prepare their console and display without guessing at the game's final graphics menus. A well-configured television can prevent avoidable display delay and crushed or washed-out detail.

sections.heading: Start with the television's actual capabilities
paragraphs: Check whether your display supports HDR, its available HDMI ports and the refresh modes enabled for the connected console. A marketing label such as 4K does not itself confirm meaningful HDR performance or low latency. Use the display manufacturer's recommended game-input settings as a starting point. Connect the console through a port that supports the desired signal and verify the console detects the expected resolution. Do not enable every picture enhancement simply because it exists; extra processing can affect responsiveness and image appearance.
points: Confirm the console is using the intended HDMI input.
Check your TV's current firmware and game-mode guidance.

sections.heading: Calibrate at the system level first
paragraphs: PlayStation and Xbox provide system display settings that can guide calibration on supported hardware. Follow the on-screen instructions under normal room lighting rather than copying someone else's brightness numbers. Adjust the TV's black level and HDR mode only when there is a clear reason, and keep notes so you can restore the baseline. A properly calibrated television can make detail more visible across different games, but it does not guarantee that a particular GTA VI scene uses an in-game HDR option. Such settings should be confirmed after release.
points: Avoid judging HDR from a compressed phone photo of another screen.
Check SDR and HDR sources separately when diagnosing a washed-out picture.

sections.heading: Treat frame rate and refresh rate separately
paragraphs: Rockstar's November 10 announcement says GTA VI targets 30 frames per second on current-generation consoles. A television capable of 120 Hz does not automatically create 120 unique game frames. Motion interpolation can make video appear smoother but may add artifacts or response delay. Try the display's low-latency game mode as a baseline and compare the same game controls with optional smoothing enabled and disabled. VRR and other HDMI features depend on the display, console and software; do not assume they guarantee a different GTA VI performance target.
points: Do not advertise a 60 FPS mode that Rockstar has not confirmed.
Keep controller and display conditions consistent when comparing responsiveness.

sections.heading: Check audio and picture without changing everything
paragraphs: A soundbar, television speaker or headset can have separate delay and output settings. If dialogue is not synchronized, identify whether the problem occurs in other games or video apps before blaming GTA VI. Likewise, a dark picture could result from the television's local settings, mismatched range options or game art direction. Change only one setting at a time and compare against a familiar scene. Keep your HDMI cable, console resolution and output mode documented so you do not create new variables during troubleshooting.
points: Compare audio timing using another known source first.
Do not use maximum sharpness as a substitute for proper signal setup.

sections.heading: Verify the released game before publishing benchmarks
paragraphs: After launch, check GTA VI's real display and accessibility menus for any game-specific controls. Technical reviews should identify the console model, game build, capture method and television mode rather than presenting a universal best settings screenshot. Rockstar has confirmed additional PS5 Pro features such as PSSR clarity and ray-traced shadows, but that does not identify every HDR slider or television combination. This guide is a setup process, not a promise of a performance increase. Update recommendations only when new measured evidence is available.
points: Compare identical scenes rather than unrelated screenshots.
Preserve a known-good display preset before experimenting.
